name: Familial GPIHBP1 Deficiency

criteria.description: Persistent severe hypertriglyceridemia with fasting triglyceride levels > 885 mg/dL (10 mmol/L)
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the GPIHBP1 gene
History of recurrent episodes of acute pancreatitis associated with hypertriglyceridemia
Exclusion of secondary causes of hypertriglyceridemia such as diabetes mellitus, alcohol use, or medications
Demonstration of chylomicronemia on lipoprotein electrophoresis or ultracentrifugation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe hypertriglyceridemia plus biallelic pathogenic GPIHBP1 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical features overlap with other familial chylomicronemia syndromes.

searchTerms: very high triglyceride levels when fasting

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes often triggered by elevated triglycerides
Yellowish papules primarily on extensor surfaces

common.notes: Milky appearance of retinal vessels on fundoscopy
Chronic discomfort due to lipid metabolism abnormalities
searchTerms: belly pain not caused by pancreatitis
nerve symptoms related to blood thickness

occasional.notes: Fatty infiltration of the liver detected by imaging
Milky or turbid plasma on blood draw
Sensory disturbances possibly due to lipid deposition
Growth retardation secondary to metabolic disturbance

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular complications such as pancreatitis-induced shock
rare.notes: Severe systemic complications secondary to pancreatitis
searchTerms: heart and blood vessel problems from pancreatitis
cardiovascular complications due to pancreas inflammation

rare.notes: Rare accumulation of chylous fluid in pleural or peritoneal spaces
Rare reports of altered immune responses

laboratory: Markedly elevated fasting triglyceride levels (>1000 mg/dL)
Normal or mildly elevated cholesterol levels
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatic steatosis
Pancreatic imaging revealing fatty infiltration or pancreatitis
other: Exclusion of secondary causes of hypertriglyceridemia

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in LPL gene instead of GPIHBP1
Similar clinical presentation but different genetic cause
Responds differently to treatment and genetic testing identifies APOC2 mutations

redFlags: Recurrent episodes of severe acute pancreatitis
Severe hypertriglyceridemia refractory to standard lipid-lowering therapy
Early onset of symptoms in infancy or childhood
references: Beigneux AP, et al. GPIHBP1 mutations and familial chylomicronemia. J Clin Invest. 2009.
Wang CS, et al. Clinical and genetic features of familial GPIHBP1 deficiency. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2021.
